note: Passage 3709 (Pro 1:16) — 'their feet run to evil.' evil (ra) read as the moral evil that is the eager destination of the wicked's haste. Descent read at full weight.

dims.v: evil — the moral wrong the wicked eagerly pursue
running to evil — the inner bent that hurries the whole person toward wrong and bloodshed
eager haste ('make haste to shed blood')
welded to bloodshed — evil here is not abstract but issues in violence

the feet 'run' — evil is figured as a bent that MOVES the person, an eager momentum toward wrong. Manner (haste) is marked here where most chars leave 108 none: the wicked's speed toward evil is the point.
